children: Stocks stumbled out of the gate this morning, led lower by the Dow industrials. Here's what is moving markets today:

Bond yields rising again: Treasurys are selling off again ahead of today's auction of 10-year notes later today, which will test demand for government debt. The benchmark 10-year yield rose to 5.32%. French government yields are also shooting higher on continuing worries about the country's fiscal health.

Fed minutes in focus: Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's September meeting will be released at 2 p.m. ET. At that meeting, the central bank raised rates for the first time in three years. In recent days, central-bank officials have suggested that they might hold rates steady at their next meeting Oct. 27-28.

Oil prices remain elevated: Crude prices are mixed today. Brent crude futures are trading above $101 a barrel, with the U.S. benchmark slipping below $90. Attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia have kept tensions elevated in the Middle East.
